correctness.rationale: At each admissible (n-1)-bit vertex the exact required imbalance is indicator(prefix 01) minus indicator(suffix 00). The F_{n-1} positive vertices contain no 00, whereas every negative vertex ends 00; source-to-sink paths necessarily use at least n-2 edges, and lexically paired overlap-one paths attain that bound. Appending zero to reach 0^{n-1}, then its added path to the no-00 core, proves connectedness of the balanced augmented graph and Euler-tour existence. The Fibonacci count of finite 001-avoiders is F_{n+3}-1. This is a complete symbolic proof for all n>=3, supplemented by reproducible checks for n<=18.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The required extra windows can be forbidden, making the proposed optimization different from a constrained de Bruijn sequence staying inside the language. Earlier general Euler-tour algorithms alone do not imply the closed formula, and related published word-cover laws for other avoided patterns do not imply it by reversal or complement.

Periodic-word Euler circuits and exact-factor-set strings do not express this all-finite-factor superset-cover optimum.

value.rationale: The all-order exact natural shortest-cover invariant is stronger than a finite table or one construction. A uniform forbidden-pattern imbalance generates a provably unavoidable (n-2)F_{n-1} overhead, asymptotically linear relative to the Fibonacci-sized target family. This gives a reusable structural obstruction and benchmark for de Bruijn and sequence-assembly problems, without an arbitrary parameter slice.
